Its abstraction level is lowered by the fact that it conditions the power on specific triggers and criteria, and by the detailed safeguards it sets for when and how that power may be exercised.

testo_originale: Article 23 Nomenclatures 1. Any references to nomenclatures in the context of public procurement shall be made using the Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) as adopted by Regulation (EC) No 2195/2002. 2. The Commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 87 to adapt the CPV codes referred to in this Directive, whenever changes in the CPV nomenclature must be reflected in this Directive and they do not imply a modification of the scope of this Directive.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-technical provision: it fixes a mandatory reference system for terminology and then delegates a limited updating power to the Commission. It sits below foundational principles because it does not set the framework’s aims or core rights, but above purely operational details because it standardises how references are made and how the text may be technically adjusted over time.

testo_originale: Article 24 Conflicts of interest Member States shall ensure that contracting authorities take appropriate measures to effectively prevent, identify and remedy conflicts of interest arising in the conduct of procurement procedures so as to avoid any distortion of competition and to ensure equal treatment of all economic operators. The concept of conflicts of interest shall at least cover any situation where staff members of the contracting authority or of a procurement service provider acting on behalf of the contracting authority who are involved in the conduct of the procurement procedure or may influence the outcome of that procedure have, directly or indirectly, a financial, economic or other personal interest which might be perceived to compromise their impartiality and independence in the context of the procurement procedure.
descrizione_funzionale: This is a structural-operational provision: it sets a general compliance duty for Member States and contracting authorities, then immediately translates that duty into a concrete minimum concept that must be covered. Its abstraction level is intermediate because it does not merely announce a principle, but it also does not descend into a detailed procedure; instead, it frames the required safeguards and defines the core scope of the concept to be applied.

testo_originale: Article 25 Conditions relating to the GPA and other international agreements In so far as they are covered by Annexes 1, 2, 4 and 5 and the General Notes to the European Union’s Appendix I to the GPA and by the other international agreements by which the Union is bound, contracting authorities shall accord to the works, supplies, services and economic operators of the signatories to those agreements treatment no less favourable than the treatment accorded to the works, supplies, services and economic operators of the Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural rule at an intermediate level: it lays down a binding equality-of-treatment standard that governs a defined category of cases, rather than a general purpose or a detailed procedure. Its abstraction is limited by the explicit reference to external instruments and covered categories, which makes it a conditional operative norm rather than a foundational principle.

testo_originale: Article 26 Choice of procedures
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision at an intermediate level: it sets the framework for how the relevant process may be conducted, rather than laying down a detailed step-by-step rule. Its function is to organise the available procedural options and the conditions for using them, so it is more general than an operational rule but less foundational than a principle-setting clause.

testo_originale: 1. When awarding public contracts, contracting authorities shall apply the national procedures adjusted to be in conformity with this Directive, provided that, without prejudice to Article 32, a call for competition has been published in accordance with this Directive.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that sets a concrete condition for how the procedure must be used in a particular case, rather than laying down a general principle. It is specific because it ties the applicable national procedure to a defined precondition — publication of a call for competition — and thus functions as a narrow implementation rule within the broader framework.

testo_originale: 2. Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply open or restricted procedures as regulated in this Directive.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision that authorizes the use of two predefined procedural models within the broader framework. It sits below foundational principles because it does not create a general rule or purpose; instead, it specifies an institutional choice and ties it to procedures already regulated elsewhere in the act.

testo_originale: 3. Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply innovation partnerships as regulated in this Directive.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision authorising a specific procedural instrument within the broader framework — it sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not state a general principle, but enables a particular mechanism to be used. Its normative role is to open the way for a defined implementation option, while leaving the detailed conditions to the surrounding rules.

testo_originale: 4. Member States shall provide that contracting authorities may apply a competitive procedure with negotiation or a competitive dialogue in the following situations:
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it authorizes the use of two alternative procedures only in specified situations, so it sits below the general framework but above purely technical implementation. Its level of abstraction is limited because it does not lay down a broad principle; instead, it conditions a procedural choice on defined circumstances.

testo_originale: (a) with regard to works, supplies or services fulfilling one or more of the following criteria:
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational qualifier introducing a conditional gateway for the application of a rule. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish a general principle or define a framework, but instead narrows the scope by listing the concrete criteria that must be met.

testo_originale: (i) the needs of the contracting authority cannot be met without adaptation of readily available solutions;
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a multi-part test, sitting toward the technical end of the spectrum. It specifies one concrete condition to be checked in applying a broader rule, rather than laying down a general principle or institutional framework.

testo_originale: (ii) they include design or innovative solutions;
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader rule, sitting near the technical end of the hierarchy. It specifies one concrete qualifying feature to be checked in a particular procedural context, rather than laying down a general principle or institutional framework.

testo_originale: (iii) the contract cannot be awarded without prior negotiations because of specific circumstances related to the nature, the complexity or the legal and financial make-up or because of the risks attaching to them;
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader procedural framework, sitting toward the technical end of the spectrum. It specifies a concrete condition that must be satisfied to justify a particular procedural route, using a fact-sensitive test tied to defined circumstances rather than laying down a general principle or structural rule.

testo_originale: (iv) the technical specifications cannot be established with sufficient precision by the contracting authority with reference to a standard, European Technical Assessment, common technical specification or technical reference within the meaning of points 2 to 5 of Annex VII;
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational exception clause within a broader procedural rule, because it triggers only when a prescribed technical benchmark cannot be formulated with sufficient precision. It functions as a narrow conditional criterion that channels how the general rule is applied in a particular case, rather than setting any overarching principle.

testo_originale: (b) with regard to works, supplies or services where, in response to an open or a restricted procedure, only irregular or unacceptable tenders are submitted. In such situations contracting authorities shall not be required to publish a contract notice where they include in the procedure all of, and only, the tenderers which satisfy the criteria set out in Articles 57 to 64 and which, during the prior open or restricted procedure, submitted tenders in accordance with the formal requirements of the procurement procedure. In particular, tenders which do not comply with the procurement documents, which were received late, where there is evidence of collusion or corruption, or which have been found by the contracting authority to be abnormally low, shall be considered as being irregular. In particular tenders submitted by tenderers that do not have the required qualifications, and tenders whose price exceeds the contracting authority’s budget as determined and documented prior to the launching of the procurement procedure shall be considered as unacceptable.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational and technical provision: it sets a narrow exception to the ordinary publication requirement and specifies the exact conditions under which that exception applies. Its abstraction level is low because it does not articulate a general principle or institutional power, but instead fixes concrete eligibility criteria and examples of irregular or unacceptable tenders within a specific procedural scenario.

testo_originale: 5. The call for competition shall be made by means of a contract notice pursuant to Article

testo_originale: 6. testo_originale: 3. Where a state of urgency duly substantiated by the contracting authority renders impracticable the time limit laid down in the second subparagraph of paragraph 1, it may fix a time limit which shall be not less than 15 days from the date on which the contract notice was sent.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational exception clause that adjusts a procedural deadline in a defined emergency scenario — it sits near the technical end of the hierarchy because it does not set a general principle, but a conditional rule for a specific case. Its key feature is that it fixes an alternative minimum time limit and ties it to a substantiated finding by the authority, making it a precise implementation rule rather than a structural norm.

testo_originale: 4. descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow conditional adjustment to a procedural deadline. testo_originale: Article 28 Restricted procedure
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision that identifies one of the core procedural modes within the framework, sitting below the general principles but above detailed implementation rules. testo_originale: 1. testo_originale: Article 29 Competitive procedure with negotiation
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision that sets out a specific procedural route within the wider framework, rather than a general principle. testo_originale: 1. In competitive procedures with negotiation, any economic operator may submit a request to participate in response to a call for competition containing the information set out in Annex V parts B and C by providing the information for qualitative selection that is requested by the contracting authority. They shall also indicate which elements of the description define the minimum requirements to be met by all tenders. The information provided shall be sufficiently precise to enable economic operators to identify the nature and scope of the procurement and decide whether to request to participate in the procedure. The minimum time limit for receipt of requests to participate shall be 30 days from the date on which the contract notice or, where a prior information notice is used as a means of calling for competition, the invitation to confirm interest was sent. The minimum time limit for the receipt of initial tenders shall be 30 days from the date on which the invitation was sent. Article 28(3) to (6) shall apply.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a strong technical character: it lays down the concrete steps, required disclosures, and minimum time limits for a specific procedural variant. Its abstraction level is low because it does not state a general principle, but instead fixes detailed procedural conditions and cross-references another article for further rule application.

testo_originale: 2. Only those economic operators invited by the contracting authority following its assessment of the information provided may submit an initial tender which shall be the basis for the subsequent negotiations. testo_originale: 4. Contracting authorities may award contracts on the basis of the initial tenders without negotiation where they have indicated, in the contract notice or in the invitation to confirm interest, that they reserve the possibility of doing so.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational clause setting a conditional rule for a specific procedural option: it authorises a direct award path only if a prior reservation has been expressly signalled in the relevant notice. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish a general principle, but instead fixes the precise condition under which a particular step may be taken.

testo_originale: 5. During the negotiations, contracting authorities shall ensure the equal treatment of all tenderers. testo_originale: 1. descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that specifies an evidentiary method and the conditions for accepting equivalent documentation, so it sits near the technical end of the spectrum. testo_originale: 2. descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow evidentiary rule: it specifies an alternative means of proof that must be accepted only in a defined contingency. Its abstraction level is low because it does not set a general principle, but instead lays down conditional criteria and a concrete procedural fallback for a specific verification situation.

testo_originale: 3. descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow cooperative function: it requires authorities to furnish specified information when another Member State requests it. testo_originale: 1. Contracting authorities may authorise or require tenderers to submit variants. descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow procedural function: it regulates when an alternative proposal may be allowed and how that choice must be signposted in the call for competition. testo_originale: 2. descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a fairly narrow scope: it regulates how an authority must handle an optional procedural feature once that option is used. Its abstraction level is low because it does not set a general principle, but instead specifies concrete documentation and evaluation requirements that must be satisfied in a defined situation.

testo_originale: 3. Only variants meeting the minimum requirements laid down by the contracting authorities shall be taken into consideration. descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational rule within a broader award procedure, sitting toward the technical end of the spectrum. testo_originale: Article 46 Division of contracts into lots

descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a moderately specific scope: it regulates how an authority may structure an award decision and imposes a limited explanatory duty when a particular option is not used. testo_originale: 2. testo_originale: 3. descrizione_funzionale: Operational clause with a narrow conditional empowerment: it authorises a specific award method only if a prior notice-based reservation has been made and the relevant lots have been identified. testo_originale: 4. descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational empowerment clause: it authorises Member States to make a specific procedural option mandatory, while leaving the concrete conditions to be fixed under national law within the limits of Union law. testo_originale: Article 49 Innovation partnership

testo_originale: (c) of Article 44(4) by providing the information for qualitative selection that is requested by the contracting entity. testo_originale: 2. testo_originale: 1. Contracting entities may conclude framework agreements, provided that they apply the procedures provided for in this Directive. A framework agreement means an agreement between one or more contracting entities and one or more economic operators, the purpose of which is to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during a given period, in particular with regard to price and, where appropriate, the quantities envisaged. The term of a framework agreement shall not exceed eight years, save in exceptional cases duly justified, in particular by the subject of the framework agreement.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that authorises a specific contracting technique and immediately conditions it on compliance with the Directive’s procedures. It also supplies a legal definition and fixes a maximum duration, which makes it a concrete implementation rule rather than a broad structural principle.

testo_originale: 2. Contracts based on a framework agreement shall be awarded on the basis of objective rules and criteria, which may include reopening the competition among those economic operators party to the framework agreement as concluded. These rules and criteria shall be set out in the procurement documents for the framework agreement. The objective rules and criteria referred to in the first subparagraph shall ensure equal treatment of the economic operators who are parties to the agreement. Where a reopening the competition is included, contracting entities shall set a time limit which is sufficiently long to allow tenders for each specific contract to be submitted and contracting entities shall award each contract to the tenderer that has submitted the best tender on the basis of the award criteria set out in the specifications of the framework agreement. Contracting entities shall not use framework agreements improperly or in such a way as to prevent, restrict or distort competition.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that lays down the concrete conditions for awarding contracts under an already-established framework arrangement. It is specific because it prescribes the required rules, timing, and award method, and adds a prohibitory safeguard against misuse, rather than setting a general principle or delegating further rule-making.

testo_originale: 2. Where contracting entities need to ensure an appropriate balance between the particular characteristics of the procurement procedure and the resources required to conduct it, they may, in restricted or negotiated procedures, in competitive dialogues or in innovation partnerships, establish objective rules and criteria that reflect this need and enable the contracting entity to reduce the number of candidates that will be invited to tender or to negotiate. The number of candidates selected shall, however, take account of the need to ensure adequate competition.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a moderately specific scope: it regulates how a contracting entity may structure candidate selection in certain named procedures. Its abstraction level is low-to-intermediate because it does not set a general principle, but instead lays down a concrete procedural option and a limiting criterion to be applied in that defined context.

testo_originale: Article 79 Reliance on the capacities of other entities
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision at an intermediate level of abstraction: it does not set a broad principle for the whole instrument, but instead organises how a participant may draw on external capacities within the framework. Its role is to allocate and condition a specific legal possibility, making it an operational gateway rule rather than a technical implementation detail.

testo_originale: 1. Where the objective rules and criteria for the exclusion and selection of economic operators requesting qualification in a qualification system include requirements relating to the economic and financial capacity of the economic operator, or to its technical and professional abilities, the economic operator may where necessary rely on the capacity of other entities, whatever the legal nature of the link between itself and those entities. With regard to criteria relating to the educational and professional qualifications of the service provider or contractor or those of the undertaking’s managerial staff or to the relevant professional experience, economic operators may however only rely on the capacities of other entities where the latter will perform the works or services for which these capacities are required. Where an economic operator wants to rely on the capacities of other entities, it shall prove to the contracting entity that those resources will be available to it throughout the period of the validity of the qualification system, for example by producing a commitment by those entities to that effect. Where, pursuant to Article 80 of this Directive, contracting entities have referred to exclusion or selection criteria provided for under Directive 2014/24/EU, contracting entities shall verify in accordance with Article 80(3) of this Directive whether the other entities on whose capacity the economic operator intends to rely fulfil the relevant selection criteria or whether there are grounds for exclusion, to which the contracting entities have referred, pursuant to Article 57 of Directive 2014/24/EU. The contracting entity shall require that the economic operator replaces an entity in respect of which there are compulsory grounds for exclusion to which the contracting entity has referred. The contracting entity may require or may be required by the Member State to require that the economic operator replaces an entity in respect of which there are non-compulsory grounds for exclusion to which the contracting entity has referred. Where an economic operator relies on the capacities of other entities with regard to criteria relating to economic and financial standing, the contracting entity may require that the economic operator and those entities be jointly liable for the execution of the contract. Under the same conditions, a group of economic operators as referred to in Article 37(2) may rely on the capacity of participants in the group or of other entities.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision at a relatively specific level: it does not set a general principle, but lays down the conditions, evidentiary requirements, and consequences for a particular qualification scenario. Its structure is technical and implementation-oriented because it details when reliance on third-party capacity is allowed, what proof is needed, and what checks or substitutions the contracting entity may require.

testo_originale: 2. Where the objective rules and criteria for the exclusion and selection of candidates and tenderers in open, restricted or negotiated procedures, in competitive dialogues or in innovation partnerships include requirements relating to the economic and financial capacity of the economic operator, or to its technical and professional abilities the economic operator may where necessary and for a particular contract rely on the capacity of other entities, whatever the legal nature of the link between itself and those entities. With regard to criteria relating to the educational and professional qualifications of the service provider or contractor or those of the undertaking’s managerial staff or to the relevant professional experience, economic operators may however only rely on the capacities of other entities where the latter will perform the works or services for which these capacities are required. Where an economic operator wants to rely on the capacities of other entities, it shall prove to the contracting entity that the necessary resources will be available to it, for example by delivering a commitment by those entities to that effect. Where, pursuant to Article 80 of this Directive, contracting entities have referred to exclusion or selection criteria provided for under Directive 2014/24/EU, contracting entities shall verify in accordance with Article 80(3) of this Directive whether the other entities on whose capacity the economic operator intends to rely fulfil the relevant selection criteria or whether there are grounds for exclusion, to which the contracting entities have referred, pursuant to Article 57 of Directive 2014/24/EU. The contracting entity shall require that the economic operator replaces an entity which does not meet a relevant selection criterion, or in respect of which there are compulsory grounds for exclusion to which the contracting entity has referred. The contracting entity may require or may be required by the Member State to require that the economic operator replaces an entity in respect of which there are non-compulsory grounds for exclusion to which the contracting entity has referred. Where an economic operator relies on the capacities of other entities with regard to criteria relating to economic and financial standing, the contracting entity may require that the economic operator and those entities be jointly liable for the execution of the contract. Under the same conditions, a group of economic operators as referred to in Article 37 may rely on the capacities of participants in the group or of other entities.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational to technical provision: it does not state a broad governing principle, but lays down a detailed mechanism for when and how an operator may rely on third-party capacities, including proof, verification, replacement, and liability consequences. Its abstraction level is low because it specifies concrete conditions and procedural steps for a particular assessment within a wider framework.

testo_originale: 3. In the case of works contracts, service contracts and siting and installation operations in the context of a supply contract, contracting entities may require that certain critical tasks be performed directly by the tenderer itself or, where the tender is submitted by a group of economic operators as referred to in Article 37(2), a participant in that group.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational clause with a narrow, situation-specific rule: it authorises contracting entities to impose a direct-performance requirement only for certain identified tasks in defined contract types. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not lay down a general principle, but instead specifies a concrete condition that may be applied within a particular procedural setting.

testo_originale: Article 80 Use of exclusion grounds and selection criteria provided for under Directive 2014/24/EU
descrizione_funzionale: Structural cross-reference clause that incorporates external rules by reference, rather than laying down a self-contained standard. It sits at an intermediate level: it organizes how this framework connects to another instrument and channels its application, but does not itself set a detailed operative test or threshold.

testo_originale: 1. The objective rules and criteria for the exclusion and selection of economic operators requesting qualification in a qualification system and the objective rules and criteria for the exclusion and selection of candidates and tenderers in open, restricted or negotiated procedures, in competitive dialogues or in innovation partnerships may include the exclusion grounds listed in Article 57 of Directive 2014/24/EU on the terms and conditions set out therein. Where the contracting entity is a contracting authority, those criteria and rules shall include the exclusion grounds listed in Article 57(1) and (2) of Directive 2014/24/EU on the terms and conditions set out in that Article. If so required by Member States, those criteria and rules shall, in addition, include the exclusion grounds listed in Article 57(4) of Directive 2014/24/EU on the terms and conditions set out in that Article.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that specifies how exclusion and selection criteria may or must be composed in particular procedural settings. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not lay down a general principle, but instead cross-references detailed conditions and mandatory inclusions that apply only in defined cases.

testo_originale: 2. The criteria and rules referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article may include the selection criteria set out in Article 58 of Directive 2014/24/EU on the terms and conditions set out therein, notably as regards the limits to requirements concerning yearly turnovers, as provided for under the second subparagraph of paragraph 3 of that Article.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that cross-references and incorporates an existing set of selection criteria, while narrowing their use through a specific condition on turnover requirements. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish a general principle or institutional structure, but instead specifies how a pre-existing rule may be applied in one defined context.

testo_originale: 3. For the purpose of applying paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, Articles 59 to 61 of Directive 2014/24/EU shall apply.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational cross-reference clause that incorporates external provisions for use in a defined application context, rather than laying down an autonomous rule. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not create a general principle; it simply directs how existing paragraphs are to be applied by importing a specific set of procedural standards.

testo_originale: Article 81 Quality assurance standards and environmental management standards
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it sits below the framework-setting level because it does not state a general principle, but instead regulates how compliance may be demonstrated through recognised standards. Its function is to specify a concrete evidentiary/verification mechanism within the broader regime, making it a targeted implementation rule rather than a foundational norm.

testo_originale: 1. Contracting entities shall, where they require the production of certificates drawn up by independent bodies attesting that the economic operator complies with certain quality assurance standards, including on accessibility for disabled persons, refer to quality assurance systems based on the relevant European standards series certified by accredited bodies. They shall recognise equivalent certificates from bodies established in other Member States. They shall also accept other evidence of equivalent quality assurance measures where the economic operator concerned had no possibility of obtaining such certificates within the relevant time limits for reasons that are not attributable to that economic operator provided that the economic operator proves that the proposed quality assurance measures comply with the required quality assurance standards.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that specifies how a contracting entity must verify compliance when it asks for proof of conformity with certain quality standards. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set the general framework or principle, but instead lays down a concrete evidentiary rule, including recognition of equivalent certificates and a fallback form of proof in a defined circumstance.

testo_originale: 2. Where contracting entities require the production of certificates drawn up by independent bodies attesting that the economic operator complies with certain environmental management systems or standards, they shall refer to the Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) of the Union or to other environmental management systems as recognised in accordance with Article 45 of Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 or other environmental management standards based on the relevant European or international standards by accredited bodies. They shall recognise equivalent certificates from bodies established in other Member States. Where an economic operator had demonstrably no access to such certificates, or no possibility of obtaining them within the relevant time limits for reasons that are not attributable to that economic operator, the contracting entity shall also accept other evidence of environmental management measures, provided that the economic operator proves that these measures are equivalent to those required under the applicable environmental management system or standard.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational rule with a technical evidentiary function, sitting near the lower end of the abstraction spectrum. It does not set a general principle or institutional structure; instead, it specifies exactly which certificates must be accepted, how equivalence is to be recognised, and what substitute proof is allowed when the usual documents cannot be obtained.

testo_originale: 3. Upon request, Member States shall make available to other Member States any information relating to the documents produced as evidence of compliance with quality and environmental standards referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision at a low-to-mid level of abstraction: it does not set a general principle, but prescribes a specific information-sharing duty triggered by a request. Its normative role is to implement a concrete procedural step within a pre-existing compliance mechanism, making it more technical than structural.

testo_originale: Article 82 Contract award criteria
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision at an intermediate level: it sets the governing rule for how awards are to be assessed, but does so in a general way rather than by prescribing a detailed procedure. Its abstraction comes from establishing the operative criterion framework for later application, without fixing a narrow technical implementation step.

testo_originale: 1. Without prejudice to national laws, regulations or administrative provisions on the price of certain supplies or the remuneration of certain services, contracting entities shall base the award of contracts on the most economically advantageous tender.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational award-rule that sets the core criterion for selecting a winner in a specific decision-making step, while expressly yielding to pre-existing national price/remuneration rules. It sits below structural principles because it does not define the framework or delegate powers; instead, it prescribes the concrete standard to be applied in contract award.

testo_originale: 2. The most economically advantageous tender from the point of view of the contracting entity shall be identified on the basis of the price or cost, using a cost-effectiveness approach, such as life-cycle costing in accordance with Article 83, and may include the best price-quality ratio, which shall be assessed on the basis of criteria, including qualitative, environmental and/or social aspects, linked to the subject-matter of the contract in question. Such criteria may comprise, for instance:
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision at a relatively specific level: it translates a general award principle into the concrete basis on which the preferred offer is to be identified. Its structure is technical because it prescribes the evaluative method and lists permissible criteria, while still leaving the detailed application to the contracting entity within defined limits.

testo_originale: (a) quality, including technical merit, aesthetic and functional characteristics, accessibility, design for all users, social, environmental and innovative characteristics and trading and its conditions;
descrizione_funzionale: Operational criterion within a broader evaluation framework, because it identifies one concrete factor to be taken into account when comparing options. It is specific and technical rather than foundational, since it does not establish the framework itself but only supplies a detailed sub-element for its application.

testo_originale: (b) organisation, qualification and experience of staff assigned to performing the contract, where the quality of the staff assigned can have a significant impact on the level of performance of the contract; or
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader evaluation rule, sitting toward the technical end of the spectrum. It specifies one concrete factor that may be assessed in a particular performance-related context, rather than laying down a general principle or structural allocation of powers.

testo_originale: (c) after-sales service and technical assistance, delivery conditions such as delivery date, delivery process and delivery period or period of completion, commitments with regard to parts and security of supply. The cost element may also take the form of a fixed price or cost on the basis of which economic operators will compete on quality criteria only. Member States may provide that contracting entities may not use price only or cost only as the sole award criterion or restrict their use to certain categories of contracting entities or certain types of contracts.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational to technical provision: it specifies concrete award-criterion elements and permissible pricing formulations, then adds a limited Member State option to constrain their use. Its placement is low on the abstraction spectrum because it does not state a general principle, but instead fixes detailed conditions for how a particular decision rule may be applied.

testo_originale: 3. Award criteria shall be considered to be linked to the subject-matter of the public contract where they relate to the works, supplies or services to be provided under that contract in any respect and at any stage of their life cycle, including factors involved in:
descrizione_funzionale: Operational definitional rule at a fairly specific level: it does not state a broad principle, but sets the criterion for when a condition is treated as sufficiently connected to the contract. Its function is to supply a legal test by describing the relevant link in abstract terms and by introducing a non-exhaustive list of life-cycle factors, making it a technical interpretive sub-rule within a broader assessment framework.

testo_originale: (a) the specific process of production, provision or trading of those works, supplies or services; or
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational criterion within a broader rule, because it isolates one concrete factor to be examined in an assessment rather than laying down a general principle. Its function is technical and sub-rule-like: it narrows the decision-making by identifying a particular aspect of the relevant activity to be checked.

testo_originale: (b) a specific process for another stage of their life cycle, even where such factors do not form part of their material substance.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational clarification within a broader definitional or assessment rule — it narrows the scope by identifying one concrete process-related factor to be taken into account at a particular stage. Its placement is technical because it does not establish a general principle or institutional power, but instead refines how an existing criterion is to be applied in a limited situation.

testo_originale: 4. Award criteria shall not have the effect of conferring an unrestricted freedom of choice on the contracting entity. They shall ensure the possibility of effective competition and shall be accompanied by specifications that allow the information provided by the tenderers to be effectively verified in order to assess how well the tenders meet the award criteria. In case of doubt, contracting entities shall verify effectively the accuracy of the information and proof provided by the tenderers.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule with a moderately specific compliance function: it constrains how a decision-making standard may be applied and requires accompanying verification measures. It sits below the structural level because it does not define the framework itself, but instead sets concrete conditions for the lawful use of a criterion in a particular assessment process.

testo_originale: 5. The contracting entity shall specify in the procurement documents, the relative weighting which it gives to each of the criteria chosen to determine the most economically advantageous tender, except where this is identified on the basis of price alone. Those weightings may be expressed by providing for a range with an appropriate maximum spread. Where weighting is not possible for objective reasons, the contracting entity shall indicate the criteria in descending order of importance.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a high degree of specificity: it prescribes exactly how the chosen evaluation criteria must be presented in the procurement documents and sets the fallback method if weighting cannot be used. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish the general framework, but instead fixes a concrete procedural requirement and an alternative ordering rule for a defined situation.

testo_originale: 1. Life-cycle costing shall to the extent relevant cover parts or all of the following costs over the life cycle of a product, service or works
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that sets a specific methodological rule for how a particular assessment may be carried out. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not establish a general principle, but instead specifies the cost components that may be included when applying that method.

testo_originale: (a) costs, borne by the contracting entity or other users, such as:

testo_originale: (i) costs relating to acquisition,
descrizione_funzionale: Highly technical operative fragment: it identifies one specific cost component within a broader calculation, without setting any general principle or autonomous rule. testo_originale: (ii) costs of use, such as consumption of energy and other resources,
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational detail within a broader evaluative list, because it identifies one concrete cost component to be taken into account rather than laying down a general principle. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum, functioning as a sub-criterion used in a particular assessment.

testo_originale: (iv) end of life costs, such as collection and recycling costs
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow technical criterion within a broader evaluative list, sitting at the operational end of the spectrum. It specifies one concrete cost component to be taken into account, rather than laying down a general principle or a structural rule.

testo_originale: (b) cost imputed to environmental externalities linked to the product, service or works during its life cycle, provided their monetary value can be determined and verified; such costs may include the cost of emissions of greenhouse gases and of other pollutant emissions and other climate change mitigation costs.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader evaluative rule, sitting near the technical end of the spectrum. It specifies a concrete cost component to be taken into account only under defined conditions, using a verifiability threshold and illustrative sub-elements rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 2. Where contracting entities assess the costs using a life-cycle costing approach, they shall indicate in the procurement documents the data to be provided by the tenderers and the method which the contracting entity will use to determine the life-cycle costs on the basis of those data. The method used for the assessment of costs imputed to environmental externalities shall fulfil all of the following conditions:
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision that translates a broader assessment rule into a concrete disclosure and calculation requirement for a specific procurement step. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it prescribes exactly what information must be stated and sets the conditions a particular method must satisfy, rather than laying down a general principle or allocating competences.

testo_originale: (a) it is based on objectively verifiable and non-discriminatory criteria. In particular where it has not been established for repeated or continuous application, it shall not unduly favour or disadvantage certain economic operators;
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule setting a concrete validity condition for a specific decision-making step, rather than a broad principle for the whole instrument. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it fixes a precise standard of assessment—objective, verifiable, and non-discriminatory criteria—and adds a targeted safeguard against undue advantage or disadvantage in a defined situation.

testo_originale: (b) it is accessible to all interested parties;
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational criterion, because it sets one concrete condition that must be satisfied within a broader procedural or substantive test. testo_originale: (c) the data required can be provided with reasonable effort by normally diligent economic operators, including economic operators from third countries party to the GPA or other international agreements by which the Union is bound.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader evidentiary rule, sitting toward the technical end of the spectrum. It specifies a concrete feasibility threshold for information provision, using a practical standard to delimit when the rule applies rather than laying down a general principle or institutional framework.

testo_originale: 3. Whenever a common method for the calculation of life-cycle costs has been made mandatory by a legislative act of the Union that common method shall be applied for the assessment of life-cycle costs. A list of such legislative acts, and where necessary the delegated acts supplementing them, is set out in Annex XV. The Commission, shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 103 concerning the update of that list, when an update of the list is necessary due to the adoption of new legislation making a common method mandatory or the repeal or modification of existing legal acts.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it sets a conditional rule for when a pre-existing Union-wide method must be used, then links that rule to an annexed list. It also delegates a limited updating power to the Commission, so it sits below foundational principles but above purely technical application details.

testo_originale: Article 84 Abnormally low tenders
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-operational provision: it sits below the framework-setting level and begins to regulate how a specific assessment is handled in practice. Its abstraction level is moderate because it does not state a general principle for the whole instrument, but instead introduces a targeted rule governing a particular evaluative step within the procedure.

testo_originale: 1. Contracting entities shall require economic operators to explain the price or costs proposed in the tender where tenders appear to be abnormally low in relation to the works, supplies or services.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision within a broader procedural framework, sitting toward the specific end of the spectrum. It triggers a concrete duty only in a defined situation and specifies the immediate step to be taken, rather than laying down a general principle or institutional arrangement.

testo_originale: 2. The explanations referred to in paragraph 1 may in particular relate to:
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational and technical: this is a narrow clarifying clause that specifies the possible content of an explanation required elsewhere, rather than laying down a general principle. Its function is to delimit and illustrate a procedural disclosure step, so it sits near the bottom of the abstraction scale as an implementation detail.

testo_originale: (a) the economics of the manufacturing process, of the services provided or of the construction method;
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow technical criterion within an assessment provision, sitting at the operational end of the hierarchy. It specifies one concrete factor to be examined, rather than laying down a general principle or allocating institutional powers.

testo_originale: (b) the technical solutions chosen or any exceptionally favourable conditions available to the tenderer for the supply of the products or services or for the execution of the work;
descrizione_funzionale: Highly specific operational criterion within a broader evaluation rule, because it isolates one concrete factor to be examined in a particular assessment. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum: it does not establish a general principle or allocate powers, but instead identifies a narrow evidentiary consideration to be checked in practice.

testo_originale: (c) the originality of the supplies, services or work proposed by the tenderer;
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader assessment framework — it sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it identifies one specific factor to be examined, rather than laying down a general principle or institutional rule. Its function is to refine how a particular evaluation is carried out in a concrete situation.

testo_originale: (d) compliance with obligations referred to in Article 36(2);
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational and technical: it is a narrow cross-reference that identifies one specific compliance element to be checked within a broader assessment. Its abstraction level is low because it does not set a general principle or define a framework, but instead inserts a precise criterion by pointing to an existing obligation elsewhere in the instrument.

testo_originale: (e) compliance with obligations referred to in Article 88;
descrizione_funzionale: Highly operational cross-reference clause, sitting near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not create a general rule itself but points to compliance with an already established obligation elsewhere in the instrument. Its function is to specify one concrete condition within a broader assessment framework, rather than to set out a foundational principle or structural allocation of powers.

testo_originale: (f) the possibility of the tenderer obtaining State aid.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational criterion within a broader assessment framework, sitting near the technical end of the spectrum. It specifies one concrete factor to be taken into account, rather than laying down a general principle or an institutional rule.

testo_originale: 3. The contracting entity shall assess the information provided by consulting the tenderer. It may only reject the tender where the evidence supplied does not satisfactorily account for the low level of price or costs proposed, taking into account the elements referred to in paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision within a broader assessment mechanism: it sets the concrete decision rule for when rejection is permitted after a specific inquiry. Its abstraction level is low because it does not establish the general framework, but instead specifies the immediate condition under which a particular procedural outcome may follow.

testo_originale: 2. Contracting entities shall reject the tender, where they have established that the tender is abnormally low because it does not comply with applicable obligations referred to in Article 36(2).
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational rule within a broader procedural framework: it prescribes a specific mandatory response once a defined condition is established. Its abstraction level is low because it does not set a general principle or define a concept, but instead fixes a concrete decision rule triggered by a particular assessment.

testo_originale: 4. Where a contracting entity establishes that a tender is abnormally low because the tenderer has obtained State aid, the tender may be rejected on that ground alone only after consultation with the tenderer where the latter is unable to prove, within a sufficient time limit fixed by the contracting entity, that the aid in question was compatible with the internal market within the meaning of Article 107 TFEU. descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule with a narrow conditional trigger: it applies only when a specific abnormality is identified and then prescribes the exact steps that must follow before rejection is allowed. Its abstraction level is low because it fixes a procedural sequence, a time limit, and a notification duty rather than stating a general principle or allocating broad powers.

testo_originale: 5. Upon request, Member States shall make available to other Member States by means of administrative cooperation any information at its disposal, such as laws, regulations, universally applicable collective agreements or national technical standards, relating to the evidence and documents produced in relation to details listed in paragraph 2.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational cooperation clause that requires Member States, on request, to provide specified categories of information to one another. It sits near the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or define a concept, but instead prescribes a concrete inter-state information-sharing mechanism triggered in a specific procedural situation.

testo_originale: Article 85 Tenders comprising products originating in third countries
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision within the framework, sitting below the foundational principles but above purely technical implementation. It sets a conditional rule for how a particular category of tenders is to be treated, so it is more specific than general principles yet still formulates a governing criterion rather than a detailed procedure.

testo_originale: 1. This Article shall apply to tenders covering products originating in third countries with which the Union has not concluded, whether multilaterally or bilaterally, an agreement ensuring comparable and effective access for Union undertakings to the markets of those third countries. It shall be without prejudice to the obligations of the Union or its Member States in respect of third countries.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision with a narrow scope condition: it activates only for a specific category of tenders defined by the absence of a reciprocal market-access agreement. Its function is technical and delimiting, because it does not lay down a general principle but instead specifies the exact circumstances in which this Article applies, while preserving higher-level external obligations.

testo_originale: 2. Any tender submitted for the award of a supply contract may be rejected where the proportion of the products originating in third countries, as determined in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 43 ) , exceeds 50 % of the total value of the products constituting the tender. For the purposes of this Article, software used in telecommunications network equipment shall be regarded as products.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational rule with a built-in quantitative threshold, sitting near the technical end of the spectrum because it governs a specific decision point in a particular award context. Its abstraction level is low because it does not set a general principle or institutional structure, but instead fixes a concrete condition for when a tender may be rejected and clarifies how one item is to be classified for that purpose.

testo_originale: 3. Subject to the second subparagraph of this paragraph, where two or more tenders are equivalent in the light of the contract award criteria defined in Article 82, preference shall be given to those tenders which may not be rejected pursuant to paragraph 2 of this Article. The prices of those tenders shall be considered equivalent for the purposes of this Article, if the price difference does not exceed 3 %. However, a tender shall not be preferred to another pursuant to the first subparagraph where its acceptance would oblige the contracting entity to acquire equipment having technical characteristics different from those of existing equipment, resulting in incompatibility, technical difficulties in operation and maintenance, or disproportionate costs.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational rule within a broader award procedure, sitting near the technical end of the spectrum because it applies only in the specific case of equivalent tenders and then resolves the tie through a defined preference rule. Its abstraction level is low because it fixes a concrete threshold and a precise exception, rather than stating a general principle or allocating institutional powers.

testo_originale: 4. For the purposes of this Article, those third countries to which the benefit of this Directive has been extended by a Council Decision in accordance with paragraph 1 shall not be taken into account for determining the proportion, referred to in paragraph 2, of products originating in third countries.
descrizione_funzionale: Narrow operational rule within a specific calculation mechanism, sitting toward the technical end of the spectrum. It does not lay down a general principle or institutional structure; instead, it excludes a defined category from a proportion-based assessment, thereby fine-tuning how an already established test is applied.

testo_originale: 5. By 31 December 2015 and every year thereafter, the Commission shall submit an annual report to the Council, on progress made in multilateral or bilateral negotiations regarding access for Union undertakings to the markets of third countries in the fields covered by this Directive, on any result which such negotiations may have achieved, and on the implementation in practice of all the agreements which have been concluded.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational reporting clause that imposes a recurring institutional duty to produce information at fixed intervals. It sits toward the technical end of the spectrum because it does not set a general principle or allocate broad powers, but instead specifies a concrete post-adoption monitoring and reporting obligation with a precise deadline and content.

testo_originale: Article 86 Relations with third countries as regards works, supplies and service contracts

testo_originale: Articolo 1 Oggetto 1. La presente direttiva stabilisce le disposizioni generali che permettono di agevolare l’esercizio della libertà di stabilimento dei prestatori nonché la libera circolazione dei servizi, assicurando nel contempo un elevato livello di qualità dei servizi stessi. 2. La presente direttiva non riguarda la liberalizzazione dei servizi d’interesse economico generale riservati a enti pubblici o privati, né la privatizzazione di enti pubblici che forniscono servizi. 3. La presente direttiva non riguarda né l’abolizione di monopoli che forniscono servizi né gli aiuti concessi dagli Stati membri cui si applicano le regole comunitarie di concorrenza. La presente direttiva lascia impregiudicata la libertà, per gli Stati membri, di definire, in conformità del diritto comunitario, quali essi ritengano essere servizi d’interesse economico generale, in che modo tali servizi debbano essere organizzati e finanziati, in conformità delle regole sugli aiuti concessi dagli Stati, e a quali obblighi specifici essi debbano essere soggetti. 4. La presente direttiva non pregiudica le misure adottate a livello comunitario o nazionale, in conformità del diritto comunitario, volte a tutelare o a promuovere la diversità culturale o linguistica o il pluralismo dei media. 5. La presente direttiva non incide sulla normativa degli Stati membri in materia di diritto penale. Tuttavia gli Stati membri non possono limitare la libertà di fornire servizi applicando disposizioni di diritto penale che disciplinano specificamente o influenzano l’accesso ad un’attività di servizi o l’esercizio della stessa, aggirando le norme stabilite nella presente direttiva. 6. La presente direttiva non pregiudica la legislazione del lavoro, segnatamente le disposizioni giuridiche o contrattuali che disciplinano le condizioni di occupazione, le condizioni di lavoro, compresa la salute e la sicurezza sul posto di lavoro, e il rapporto tra datori di lavoro e lavoratori, che gli Stati membri applicano in conformità del diritto nazionale che rispetta il diritto comunitario. Parimenti, la presente direttiva non incide sulla normativa degli Stati membri in materia di sicurezza sociale. 7. La presente direttiva non pregiudica l’esercizio dei diritti fondamentali quali riconosciuti dagli Stati membri e dal diritto comunitario, né il diritto di negoziare, concludere ed eseguire accordi collettivi e di intraprendere azioni sindacali in conformità del diritto e delle prassi nazionali che rispettano il diritto comunitario.
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational-to-structural provision that sets the directive’s overall scope, purpose, and principal exclusions. It sits high in the hierarchy because it frames the general regulatory architecture and delineates what remains outside the instrument, rather than prescribing an operational procedure or technical rule.

testo_originale: Articolo 2 Campo di applicazione 1. La presente direttiva si applica ai servizi forniti da prestatori stabiliti in uno Stato membro. 2. La presente direttiva non si applica alle attività seguenti: a) i servizi non economici d’interesse generale; b) i servizi finanziari quali l’attività bancaria, il credito, l’assicurazione e la riassicurazione, le pensioni professionali o individuali, i titoli, gli investimenti, i fondi, i servizi di pagamento e quelli di consulenza nel settore degli investimenti, compresi i servizi di cui all’allegato I della direttiva 2006/48/CE; c) i servizi e le reti di comunicazione elettronica nonché le risorse e i servizi associati in relazione alle materie disciplinate dalle direttive 2002/19/CE, 2002/20/CE, 2002/21/CE, 2002/22/CE e 2002/58/CE; d) i servizi nel settore dei trasporti, ivi compresi i servizi portuali, che rientrano nell’ambito di applicazione del titolo V del trattato CE; e) i servizi delle agenzie di lavoro interinale; f) i servizi sanitari, indipendentemente dal fatto che vengano prestati o meno nel quadro di una struttura sanitaria e a prescindere dalle loro modalità di organizzazione e di finanziamento sul piano nazionale e dalla loro natura pubblica o privata; g) i servizi audiovisivi, ivi compresi i servizi cinematografici, a prescindere dal modo di produzione, distribuzione e trasmissione, e i servizi radiofonici; h) le attività di azzardo che implicano una posta di valore pecuniario in giochi di fortuna, comprese le lotterie, i giochi d’azzardo nei casinò e le scommesse; i) le attività connesse con l’esercizio di pubblici poteri di cui all’articolo 45 del trattato; j) i servizi sociali riguardanti gli alloggi popolari, l’assistenza all'infanzia e il sostegno alle famiglie ed alle persone temporaneamente o permanentemente in stato di bisogno, forniti dallo Stato, da prestatori incaricati dallo Stato o da associazioni caritative riconosciute come tali dallo Stato; k) i servizi privati di sicurezza; l) i servizi forniti da notai e ufficiali giudiziari nominati con atto ufficiale della pubblica amministrazione. 3. La presente direttiva non si applica al settore fiscale.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural scope-defining provision at an intermediate level of abstraction: it sets the directive’s general field of application and then carves out a series of express exclusions. It is not foundational because it does not state the framework’s purpose or principles, but it is broader than an operational rule because it determines the outer boundaries within which all later provisions operate.

testo_originale: Articolo 3 Relazione con le altre disposizioni del diritto comunitario 1. Se disposizioni della presente direttiva confliggono con disposizioni di altri atti comunitari che disciplinano aspetti specifici dell’accesso ad un’attività di servizi o del suo esercizio in settori specifici o per professioni specifiche, le disposizioni di questi altri atti comunitari prevalgono e si applicano a tali settori o professioni specifiche. Tra tali atti comunitari rientrano: a) la direttiva 96/71/CE; b) il regolamento (CEE) n. 1408/71; c) la direttiva 89/552/CEE del Consiglio del 3 ottobre 1989 relativa al coordinamento di determinate disposizioni legislative, regolamentari e amministrative degli Stati membri concernenti l'esercizio delle attività televisive ( 23 ) ; d) la direttiva 2005/36/CE. 2. La presente direttiva non riguarda le norme di diritto internazionale privato, in particolare quelle che disciplinano la legge applicabile alle obbligazioni contrattuali ed extracontrattuali, ivi comprese quelle che garantiscono che i consumatori beneficeranno della tutela riconosciuta loro dalla normativa sulla protezione dei consumatori vigente nel loro Stato membro. 3. Gli Stati membri applicano le disposizioni della presente direttiva nel rispetto delle norme del trattato che disciplinano il diritto di stabilimento e la libera circolazione dei servizi.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural conflict-of-laws and scope clause that positions this act within the broader legal order by setting priority rules and exclusions. It sits at an intermediate level of abstraction because it does not create a concrete procedure or threshold, but instead determines how the act interacts with other instruments and the general treaty framework.

testo_originale: Articolo 4 Definizioni Ai fini della presente direttiva si intende per: 1) «servizio»: qualsiasi attività economica non salariata di cui all’articolo 50 del trattato fornita normalmente dietro retribuzione; 2) «prestatore»: qualsiasi persona fisica, avente la cittadinanza di uno Stato membro, o qualsiasi persona giuridica di cui all’articolo 48 del trattato, stabilita in uno Stato membro, che offre o fornisce un servizio; 3) «destinatario»: qualsiasi persona fisica che sia cittadino di uno Stato membro o che goda di diritti conferitile da atti comunitari o qualsiasi persona giuridica, di cui all’articolo 48 del trattato, stabilita in uno Stato membro che, a scopo professionale o per altri scopi, fruisce o intende fruire di un servizio; 4) «Stato membro di stabilimento»: lo Stato membro nel cui territorio è stabilito il prestatore del servizio considerato; 5) «stabilimento»: l’esercizio effettivo di un’attività economica di cui all’articolo 43 del trattato a tempo indeterminato da parte del prestatore, con un’infrastruttura stabile a partire dalla quale viene effettivamente svolta l’attività di prestazione di servizi; 6) «regime di autorizzazione»: qualsiasi procedura che obbliga un prestatore o un destinatario a rivolgersi ad un’autorità competente allo scopo di ottenere una decisione formale o una decisione implicita relativa all’accesso ad un’attività di servizio o al suo esercizio; 7) «requisito»: qualsiasi obbligo, divieto, condizione o limite stabilito dalle disposizioni legislative, regolamentari o amministrative degli Stati membri o derivante dalla giurisprudenza, dalle prassi amministrative, dalle regole degli organismi e ordini professionali o dalle regole collettive di associazioni o organizzazioni professionali adottate nell’esercizio della propria autonomia giuridica; le norme stabilite dai contratti collettivi negoziati dalle parti sociali non sono considerate di per sé come requisiti ai sensi della presente direttiva; 8) «motivi imperativi d’interesse generale»: motivi riconosciuti come tali dalla giurisprudenza della Corte di giustizia, tra i quali: l’ordine pubblico, la sicurezza pubblica, l’incolumità pubblica, la sanità pubblica, il mantenimento dell’equilibrio finanziario del sistema di sicurezza sociale, la tutela dei consumatori, dei destinatari di servizi e dei lavoratori, l’equità delle transazioni commerciali, la lotta alla frode, la tutela dell’ambiente, incluso l’ambiente urbano, la salute degli animali, la proprietà intellettuale, la conservazione del patrimonio nazionale storico ed artistico, gli obiettivi di politica sociale e di politica culturale; 9) «autorità competente»: qualsiasi organo o qualsiasi istituzione responsabile, in uno Stato membro, del controllo o della disciplina delle attività di servizi, in particolare le autorità amministrative, ivi compresi gli organi giurisdizionali che agiscono in tale veste, gli ordini professionali e le associazioni o organismi professionali che, nell’ambito della propria autonomia giuridica, disciplinano collettivamente l’accesso alle attività di servizi o il loro esercizio; 10) «Stato membro nel quale è prestato il servizio»: lo Stato membro in cui il servizio è fornito da un prestatore stabilito in un altro Stato membro; 11) «professione regolamentata»: un’attività professionale o un insieme di attività professionali ai sensi dell’articolo 3, paragrafo 1, lettera a), della direttiva 2005/36/CE; 12) «comunicazione commerciale»: qualsiasi forma di comunicazione destinata a promuovere, direttamente o indirettamente, beni, servizi, o l’immagine di un’impresa, di un’organizzazione o di una persona che svolge un’attività commerciale, industriale o artigianale o che esercita una professione regolamentata. Non costituiscono, di per sé, comunicazioni commerciali le informazioni seguenti: a) le informazioni che permettono l’accesso diretto all’attività dell’impresa, dell’organizzazione o della persona, in particolare un nome di dominio o un indirizzo di posta elettronica, b) le comunicazioni relative ai beni, ai servizi o all’immagine dell’impresa, dell’organizzazione o della persona elaborate in modo indipendente, in particolare se fornite in assenza di un corrispettivo economico.
descrizione_funzionale: Highly foundational within the act’s internal structure, because it supplies the core interpretive vocabulary that all later provisions depend on. It does not regulate conduct directly; instead, it defines key terms and boundary concepts, thereby setting the conceptual framework for the rest of the directive.

testo_originale: Articolo 5 Semplificazione delle procedure 1. Gli Stati membri esaminano le procedure e le formalità relative all’accesso ad un’attività di servizi ed al suo esercizio. Laddove le procedure e formalità esaminate ai sensi del presente paragrafo non sono sufficientemente semplici, gli Stati membri le semplificano. 2. La Commissione può stabilire formulari armonizzati a livello comunitario conformemente alla procedura di cui all’articolo 40, paragrafo 2. Tali formulari sono equivalenti ai certificati, agli attestati e a tutti gli altri documenti richiesti ai prestatori. 3. Gli Stati membri che chiedono ad un prestatore o ad un destinatario di fornire un certificato, un attestato o qualsiasi altro documento comprovante il rispetto di un particolare requisito, accettano i documenti rilasciati da un altro Stato membro che abbiano finalità equivalenti o dai quali risulti che il requisito in questione è rispettato. Essi non impongono la presentazione di documenti rilasciati da un altro Stato membro sotto forma di originale, di copia conforme o di traduzione autenticata salvo i casi previsti da altre norme comunitarie o salvo le eccezioni giustificate da motivi imperativi d’interesse generale, fra cui l’ordine pubblico e la sicurezza. Il primo comma non pregiudica il diritto degli Stati membri di richiedere traduzioni non autenticate di documenti in una delle loro lingue ufficiali. 4. Il paragrafo 3 non si applica ai documenti cui fanno riferimento l'articolo 7, paragrafo 2 e l’articolo 50 della direttiva 2005/36/CE, gli articoli 45, paragrafo 3, 46, 49 e 50 della direttiva 2004/18/CE del Parlamento europeo e del Consiglio del 31 marzo 2004 relativa al coordinamento delle procedure di aggiudicazione degli appalti pubblici di lavori, di forniture e di servizi ( 24 ) , l’articolo 3, paragrafo 2 della direttiva 98/5/CE del Parlamento europeo e del Consiglio del 16 febbraio 1998 volta a facilitare l’esercizio permanente della professione di avvocato in uno Stato membro diverso da quello in cui è stata acquistata la qualifica ( 25 ) , la direttiva 68/151/CEE del Consiglio del 9 marzo 1968, intesa a coordinare, per renderle equivalenti, le garanzie che sono richieste negli Stati membri alle società a monte dell'articolo 58, secondo comma, del trattato per proteggere gli interessi dei soci e dei terzi ( 26 ) e la undicesima direttiva 89/666/CEE del Consiglio del 21 dicembre 1989 relativa alla pubblicità delle succursali create in uno Stato membro da taluni tipi di società soggette al diritto di un altro Stato ( 27 ) .
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it sits below broad framework principles but above purely technical implementation, because it organizes how procedures must be handled and how documents are to be accepted across cases. Its level of abstraction is driven by a mix of general procedural obligations and a few concrete exceptions and delegations, which make it more specific than a foundational clause but not merely a terminal technical detail.

testo_originale: Articolo 7 Diritto all’informazione 1. Gli Stati membri provvedono affinché per il tramite degli sportelli unici i prestatori e i destinatari possano agevolmente prendere conoscenza delle informazioni seguenti: a) i requisiti applicabili ai prestatori stabiliti sul territorio di uno Stato membro, in particolare quelli relativi alle procedure e alle formalità da espletare per accedere alle attività di servizi ed esercitarle; b) i dati necessari per entrare direttamente in contatto con le autorità competenti, compresi quelli delle autorità competenti in materia di esercizio delle attività di servizi; c) i mezzi e le condizioni di accesso alle banche dati e ai registri pubblici relativi ai prestatori ed ai servizi; d) i mezzi di ricorso esistenti in genere in caso di controversie tra le autorità competenti ed il prestatore o il destinatario, o tra un prestatore ed un destinatario, o tra prestatori; e) i dati di associazioni o organizzazioni diverse dalle autorità competenti presso le quali i prestatori o i destinatari possono ottenere assistenza pratica. 2. Gli Stati membri provvedono affinché i prestatori e i destinatari possano beneficiare, su richiesta, dell’assistenza delle autorità competenti, che consiste nel fornire informazioni sul modo in cui i requisiti di cui al paragrafo 1, lettera a), vengono generalmente interpretati ed applicati. Ove opportuno, tale assistenza include una semplice guida esplicativa. L’informazione è fornita in un linguaggio semplice e comprensibile. 3. Gli Stati membri provvedono affinché le informazioni e l’assistenza di cui ai paragrafi 1 e 2 siano fornite in modo chiaro e non ambiguo, siano facilmente accessibili a distanza e per via elettronica e siano aggiornate. 4. Gli Stati membri provvedono affinché gli sportelli unici e le autorità competenti rispondano con la massima sollecitudine alle domande di informazioni o alle richieste di assistenza di cui ai paragrafi 1 e 2 e, in caso di richiesta irregolare o infondata, ne informino senza indugio il richiedente. 5. Gli Stati membri e la Commissione adottano misure di accompagnamento volte ad incoraggiare gli sportelli unici a rendere accessibili le informazioni di cui al presente articolo in altre lingue comunitarie. Ciò non pregiudica la legislazione degli Stati membri in materia di impiego delle lingue. 6. L’obbligo, per le autorità competenti, di assistere i prestatori e i destinatari non impone a tali autorità di prestare consulenza legale in singoli casi ma riguarda soltanto un’informazione generale sul modo in cui i requisiti sono di norma interpretati e applicati.
descrizione_funzionale: This is a structural-to-operational provision: it does not set a broad principle alone, but translates an access-to-information guarantee into concrete administrative duties for Member States and competent bodies. Its level is relatively specific because it fixes the channels, content, quality standards, response timing, and a limiting clarification on the scope of assistance, making it an implementation rule rather than a foundational norm.

testo_originale: Articolo 8 Procedure per via elettronica 1. Gli Stati membri provvedono affinché le procedure e le formalità relative all’accesso ad un'attività di servizio e al suo esercizio possano essere espletate con facilità, a distanza e per via elettronica, mediante lo sportello unico e le autorità competenti. 2. Il paragrafo 1 non riguarda i controlli del luogo in cui il servizio è prestato o delle attrezzature utilizzate dal prestatore, o l’esame fisico dell'idoneità o dell'integrità personale di quest’ultimo o del suo personale responsabile. 3. La Commissione adotta, secondo la procedura di cui all’articolo 40, paragrafo 2, le modalità d’applicazione del paragrafo 1 del presente articolo al fine di agevolare l’interoperabilità dei sistemi di informazione e l’uso di procedure per via elettronica fra Stati membri, tenendo conto di standard comuni stabiliti a livello comunitario.
descrizione_funzionale: Structural-to-operational provision: it sets an implementation requirement for Member States and then carves out a specific exception, so it is more concrete than a general principle but still not purely technical. The final sentence is a delegated implementing clause, because it authorizes the Commission to adopt detailed application rules to facilitate interoperability and electronic procedures, which places the segment toward the operational end of the hierarchy.

testo_originale: Articolo 9 Regimi di autorizzazione 1. Gli Stati membri possono subordinare l’accesso ad un’attività di servizio e il suo esercizio ad un regime di autorizzazione soltanto se sono soddisfatte le condizioni seguenti: a) il regime di autorizzazione non è discriminatorio nei confronti del prestatore; b) la necessità di un regime di autorizzazione è giustificata da un motivo imperativo di interesse generale; c) l’obiettivo perseguito non può essere conseguito tramite una misura meno restrittiva, in particolare in quanto un controllo a posteriori interverrebbe troppo tardi per avere reale efficacia. 2. Nella relazione prevista all’articolo 39, paragrafo 1, gli Stati membri indicano i propri regimi di autorizzazione e ne motivano la conformità al paragrafo 1 del presente articolo. 3.
